questions.title: String Hash to a Slot
questions.description:
A simple hash function for keys is the sum of character codes modulo the table size.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int hash_key(const char *key)

It must return (sum of the character codes of key) % 101.

Input Format:
One token (the key).

Output Format:
One line with the slot number 0..100.

Constraints:
1 <= length of key <= 99, key contains only lowercase letters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of key <= 99, key contains only lowercase letters

questions.title: Integer Hash to a Slot
questions.description:
Integer keys usually hash straight into the table with the modulo operator.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int hash_int(int v)

It must return v % 101.

Input Format:
One line with the integer key.

Output Format:
One line with the slot number 0..100.

Constraints:
0 <= v <= 1000000

questions.title: Frequency of a Target Value
questions.description:
Counting occurrences of a value is the bread and butter of frequency tables.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_target(const int *arr, int n, int target)

It must return how many times target appears in arr.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Lookup: Is the Key Present
questions.description:
A hash table answers membership queries; here you do the direct scan version.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int contains(const int *arr, int n, int target)

It must return 1 if target appears in arr, and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Any Duplicate Present
questions.description:
The first thing a duplicate detector asks: does this collection contain any repeated value at all?

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_duplicate(const int *arr, int n)

It must return 1 if some value appears at least twice, and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Collision Slot Check
questions.description:
Two keys collide when they hash into the same slot of a 101-slot table.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int same_slot(int a, int b)

It must return 1 when a % 101 equals b % 101, and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO.

Input Format:
One line with two integer keys.

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 1000000

Line 1: n, the number of log entries.
Line 2: n space-separated track ids.
Line 3: track.

One line with the play count.

questions.title: Locker Slot Assignment
questions.description:
A school maps each student id to one of 101 cabinets with slot = studentId % 101.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int locker_slot(int studentId)

It must return studentId % 101.

Input Format:
One line with the student id.

Output Format:
One line with the cabinet number 0..100.

Constraints:
0 <= studentId <= 1000000

questions.title: Busy Slots in the Locker Room
questions.description:
Given a batch of locker assignments, count how many distinct cabinets are occupied (two students with the same slot share the collision).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int occupied_slots(const int *ids, int n)

It must return the number of distinct values among the slots id % 101. Marking a seen[] table of size 101 is the hash-table way to do it.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated student ids.

Output Format:
One line with the occupied slot count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= student ids <= 1000000

questions.title: First Duplicate in a Scan
questions.description:
A warehouse scanner reads item codes; the alarm fires on the first value that appears a second time. Report that value (the one whose second occurrence comes earliest).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int first_duplicate(const int *arr, int n)

It must return the value whose second occurrence has the smallest index, or -1 when every value is unique. Item codes are in the range 1..n, so a seen[] table keyed by value works in one pass.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated item codes.

Output Format:
One line with the first duplicate value or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= arr[i] <= n

questions.title: Transaction Pairs with a Target Sum
questions.description:
A fraud detector counts unordered index pairs (i < j) whose transaction amounts add up to a target. A frequency table over the bounded values makes this a single pass.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_pairs(const int *arr, int n, int target)

It must return the number of pairs i < j with arr[i] + arr[j] == target. Values lie in [-50, 50], so a freq[] table of size 101 with a +50 offset covers every complement.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated amounts.
Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the pair count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -50 <= arr[i] <= 50, -100 <= target <= 100

questions.title: Letter Frequency Histogram
questions.description:
A text profiler prints a histogram of the letters that occur in a word: every letter a-z that appears at least once, in alphabetical order, as "letter:count".

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void char_counts(const char *s, int *out)

It must fill out[0..25] with the counts of 'a'..'z' (0 for absent letters). The harness prints the "letter:count" entries with a positive count.

Input Format:
One token of lowercase letters.

Output Format:
One line with entries like "a:3 b:1", space-separated, in a-to-z order.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999, s contains only 'a'-'z'
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of s <= 999, s contains only 'a'-'z'

It must return the value with the highest frequency. Values lie in [-50, 50], so a freq[] table with a +50 offset works.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated sensor values.

Output Format:
One line with the most frequent value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -50 <= arr[i] <= 50

questions.title: Pharmacy Label Anagram Check
questions.description:
A pharmacy verifies that a medicine label is a rearrangement of the prescription code (same letters, any order). Counting letters with a frequency table answers it in O(length).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_anagram(const char *a, const char *b)

It must return 1 when a and b are anagrams of each other (both lowercase, equal lengths), and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO.

Input Format:
One line with two lowercase tokens a and b (same length).

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= lengths <= 99, both tokens contain only 'a'-'z'

questions.title: Distinct Inventory Codes
questions.description:
A stock report needs the number of distinct codes in a shipment. With bounded codes, a seen[] table replaces any heavyweight set.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int distinct_count(const int *arr, int n)

It must return the number of distinct values in arr. Values lie in [-50, 50]; mark a seen[] table with a +50 offset and count marked entries.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated codes.

Output Format:
One line with the distinct count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -50 <= arr[i] <= 50

questions.title: Fraud Pair: Two-Sum Indices
questions.description:
A fraud engine flags exactly one pair of transactions whose amounts sum to a target. Report their indices (smallest first) using a single left-to-right pass with a seen[] lookup table.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void two_sum(const int *arr, int n, int target, int *out)

It must store the earlier index into out[0] and the later index into out[1]. Exactly one such pair exists in every test. Amounts lie in [-100, 100], so seen[v + 100] can hold the index (plus one) of the first occurrence of each value.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated amounts.
Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the two indices (earlier first), space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100 <= arr[i] <= 100, -200 <= target <= 200, exactly one valid pair exists
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, -100 <= arr[i] <= 100, -200 <= target <= 200, exactly one valid pair exists

questions.title: Union and Intersection Counts
questions.description:
An analytics job reports how many distinct values the union and the intersection of two customer sets contain. Both arrays hold distinct values in [-50, 50], so two frequency tables with a +50 offset answer everything.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void union_intersection(const int *a, int n, const int *b, int m, int *out)

It must store the union size into out[0] and the intersection size into out[1] (distinct values in both cases).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n distinct values of the first set.
Line 3: m.
Line 4: m distinct values of the second set.

Output Format:
One line with the union size, then the intersection size, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 1000, -50 <= values <= 50, values within each array are distinct
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n, m <= 1000, -50 <= values <= 50, values within each array are distinct

questions.title: Longest Consecutive Version Run
questions.description:
Firmware build numbers arrive out of order; QA wants the length of the longest run of consecutive integers present anywhere in the batch (order in the input does not matter). Values lie in [-100, 100] — mark a seen[] table and scan it.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int longest_consecutive(const int *arr, int n)

It must return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers (e.g. 3,4,5) such that every element of the sequence appears in arr.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated build numbers.

Output Format:
One line with the longest consecutive run length.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100 <= arr[i] <= 100

questions.title: Sensor Drift: Subarrays with Target Sum
questions.description:
A sensor stream may drift negative; QA counts how many contiguous windows sum exactly to a calibration constant k. Prefix sums plus a frequency table (with a +10000 offset) solve it in one pass.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int subarray_sum_count(const int *arr, int n, int k)

It must return the number of pairs (l <= r) with arr[l] + ... + arr[r] == k. Readings lie in [-20, 20] and n <= 500, so every prefix sum stays within [-10000, 10000].

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated readings.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500, -20 <= arr[i] <= 20, -200 <= k <= 200
